text:
(4) In applying subsection (2) by reference to any given time the state of affairs at that
time (including the case for the prosecution as it stands at that time) must be taken
into account.

(5) Where the accused gives a defence statement under section 5, 6 or 6B—
(a) if as a result of that statement the prosecutor is required by this section to make
any disclosure, or further disclosure, he must do so during the period which,
by virtue of section 12, is the relevant period for this section;
(b) if the prosecutor considers that he is not so required, he must during that period
give to the accused a written statement to that effect.

(6) For the purposes of this section prosecution material is material—
(a) which is in the prosecutor’s possession and came into his possession in
connection with the case for the prosecution against the accused, or
(b) which, in pursuance of a code operative under Part 2, he has inspected in
connection with the case for the prosecution against the accused.
